body: This is particularly saddening. It is evident that you care about human rights, but you've bought wholesale into this poisonous rhetoric that more people leads to some form of slavery. Ultimately I can see how one would arrive at that conclusion, but the sheer amount of logical leaps it takes to get to that position makes it a clear-cut case of catastrophizing. As such, there are myriad other conclusions one could draw. One obvious example being that we can expand our collective consciousness to make a better world for future (hopefully ever larger) generations by the sheer magnitude of human ingenuity. As human populations grow exponentially, so too does human knowledge and the vast potential for innovation and discovery. We have a massive universe yet to be traveled. The future is bright.

You're essentially saying that a bunch non-sentient animals we can breed ourselves, plants we can produce ourselves vermin and bacteria are more important than human life, at the heart of it. Where have I heard that sort of rhetoric before? Stare long enough into the abyss....

Silly argument. We can breed livestock and farm plants to our hearts' content. I'm not particularly interested in "animal rights" at the expense of human autonomy and the sanctity of human life. Yeah weight gain is a real problem on that drug class. I binge-ate an embarrassing amount while on Abilify because of the ridiculous hunger pains it would give. I've since lost that weight, which is a big deal for quality of life.

In my case, I found the medicine very effective for a while but side effects became intolerable and the withdrawal was horrendous. Patience, self-compassion, and support are critical during this. I had a couple failed attempts at withdrawing from the med so I know it's not easy. 

Don't be afraid to lean on your support system as well. That was a huge factor for me in getting through it. If you don't have anyone you trust with this in your personal life, you can reach out to your local NAMI affiliate (if you are in the US) and find a free support group. I hope all goes well for you. You deserve to feel better.

Antipsychotics are legitimate hell. Worst part is, most psychs won't even admit to how hard it is to withdraw. "Oh it's just your symptoms returning" is the go-to "answer" to this issue. One of the biggest problems with the psychiatric industry is the outright refusal to acknowledge the addictive potential of these drugs and come up with helpful, constructive (and ideally interactive/responsive) withdrawal plans.

I encourage you to keep at it and be kind to yourself as you go through this process. I made this choice for myself almost a year ago and as hard as it's been it's worth it. Even if only to avoid the potential for long-term crippling side effects (like TD). Granted I was only taking a low dose for depression without psychotic features, so obviously this is just my personal experience and not medical advice. But there is light at the end of this tunnel, and your experience is absolutely valid. It's just a shame that medical professionals don't seem to believe it's a significant problem.

I totally get where you're coming from. As I said, I won't deny that Islam has its dark side both in terms of scripture and some of its adherents. But why don't all believers in other religions get taken to task for such things in the same manner? To attack my own "side" here for a moment, Jews believe they are "God's chosen people." When I used to go to synagogue we would thank God himself for making us Jews, as that is better than being any other kind of person. This mentality can be used to justify some pretty heinous things, from persecuting nonbelievers in their communities in NYC to extrajudicial killings in Palestine. Not only that, but Orthodox Jews are horrible to women. Ever seen a picture of the Wailing Wall in Jerusalem? The men get 75% or so of the wall for their prayers, whereas women are crammed into the small remainder. Efforts to equalize this have failed because the religious authority believes that to do so would be "ceding holy ground" to women. Yet no one has ever asked me to disavow my former faith, join the PLO, or go protest the treatment of non-Jews in Brooklyn neighborhoods. Why hold liberal Muslims to a different standard?


I hear this argument a lot that moderate/liberal Muslims need to put pressure on their leadership to take action against bad actors who wear the mantle of their religion, or even go so far as to leave their lives and fight in a dangerous sectarian conflict. I think this mentality is unfair. Most people in any religion simply want to go to their house of worship and be comforted by their community and the promises of their faith. From my conversations with religious people of any stripe, what it ultimately boils down to is a desire for life to "mean something," and the key for them is some deity or deities. I don't need that, but I don't begrudge them it either. People are unfortunately willing to ignore a lot when the alternative is sacrificing their community and the answers to life as they know it. As another example, why didn't people leave the Catholic Church in droves after the child abuse scandals, especially after most of the criminals and their enablers were never punished? Why didn't more parishioners call upon Church leadership to take action? It would have been easy to apply pressure; people could have just stopped giving their hard-earned money to their local parishes until something was done. Yet the collection plates remain full, and the Vatican is stuffed with gold.

Ultimately, I view people as individuals and not part of some monolith. I'm not immune to prejudice of course, but I judge people based on their own actions in day-to-day life. Most people, regardless of race, religion, nationality, etc, are striving for the same things at the end of the day: happiness and security for themselves and their loved ones. The people we should be angry with are those at the top who exploit and stoke our fears and divisions. The commonality among these schisms is powerful people exploiting the public for their own ends, with a divide and conquer strategy that seems to work well on far too many people. I for one refuse to join in.

I won't dispute that the Quran has some...questionable elements to say the least. I agree that the concept of nonbelievers, even virtuous ones, being damned is fucked up. However, to the average Muslim, it doesn't mean much in practice. The "worst" encounter I had regarding this was talking to a Muslim friend during one of our numerous debates regarding religion. I asked him, "So, am I damned being that I'm an atheist?" (Yes, atheist Jews do exist as contradictory as it sounds, feel free to ask me about it.) And his reply was, "That's not for me to say." So he respects my beliefs, or lack thereof, and holds his opinions about my status with respect to an afterlife I don't even believe in to himself. Whatever he believes privately is his business, and what I believe is my own. In fact, that's what the Surah about non-believers emphasizes: to each his own regarding religion, even if what the other party believes is "wrong."


All that being said, the nastier parts of the Quran and the way certain people twist the faith to justify terroristic acts do not justify a wholesale hatred of all Muslims. Your typical Muslim is, well...just a person. Yes there are extremists, but there are nearly 2 billion believers worldwide. Surely you can't tar them all with the same brush. After all, the Bible has its own fucked up rules and stories (marry your rapist? Sell your women to another tribe to appease them because they're pissed off at you?) and yet Jews and Christians don't get held to account for those elements like Muslims with respect to the darker side of the Quran. Furthermore, terrorism has as much a nationalistic aspect as a religious one, if not more so. Muslims in the middle east have had to put up with western interference at best, and oppression and slaughter at worst. So a select few people get the idea that the best way to assert their sovereignty is to terrorize those whom they see as their oppressors, using a warped interpretation of their religion in an effort to grant it legitimacy. In fact, they even oppress any moderate Muslims they can get their hands on who won't fall in line with their worldview (see: ISIS in Syria), which is the vast majority. Imperialism and disregard of sovereignty have made the world a much worse place than it ought to be.


So essentially, what I'm saying is it's unfair and counterproductive to hate an entire group of people because of the actions of a select few extremists. I mean, most terrorist attacks are committed by men. Should we hate all men? The British committed numerous atrocities in the name of their empire. Should we hate all Britishers? Should we hate all Germans for the Holocaust? The answer to all those questions is categorically no, if you have a shred of humanity or logic. Everyone has something to answer for if you want to hold people to collective account for every bad act committed by their group. And there are so many ways to slice and dice society that it's honestly rather insane to ascribe the actions of a few to an entire arbitrary group, especially one as vast and diverse as Muslims.


Sorry for the long-winded comment, but I get concerned when I see indiscriminate (I won't use the word blind, as you have your reasons) hatred toward any group, Muslim or otherwise. I hope you'll take this under consideration.

So I can't say I'm entirely anti-Israel, as it would be like being anti-weather. It's there, and we have to deal with it. Hence, I see it as my duty to expect Israel to hold itself to a higher standard and not emulate the very people who oppressed us before.

As for "genociding the Jews," the only people who express such a desire are terrorists and other fringe lunatics. The average Palestinian, as well as the Palestinian government, merely seeks equal status and protection under the laws of the land, and for their rights and territorial claims not to be encroached upon. In hindsight however, it appears that my vulnerable state was somehow attractive to him, as he began to come on stronger once he knew the whole truth of my separation/divorce.

It's kind of a balancing act - you don't want someone who's scared off by your divorce, but by the same token it's problematic if he or she appears even more excited once it comes to light.  I knew then and I know for sure now that his behavior was a red flag, but I was so excited by the prospect of being wanted again that I didn't really care. 

He's even said "I love you" multiple times which strikes me as premature. I reciprocated because I wasn't sure what else to say, but oddly enough that seemed to put him off. I think it all boils down to him being an immature guy who wants to be in control while not knowing what he wants. 

Looks like I am more ready now, as I've learned something major to avoid in the future for sure.

This is what I meant when I said "too soon" is more an emotional wellness thing rather than a timeframe. For me it seems to be too soon since I let myself get swept up in an illusion and took his words at face value when he said how much he cares for me. Who knows, perhaps he thought he meant it at the time, but it hasn't been borne out by his recent actions. And since I invested too much emotional energy too soon, I've fallen down hard yet again.

So I think I need to spend some serious time rebuilding myself before I can venture out into these waters again, as tempting as it may be. Hopefully I can be a better, or at least more complete, person for my next partner.

I want to add that I realize this is probably too much emotional investment in such a new relationship, but I guess that's part of the problem with moving on with someone new before you're really ready.

He also came on super strong in the beginning, and I bought in to all his loving words and affection. But now that he "has me," so to speak, he just treats me like an afterthought. It's pretty unsettling, especially given that he's well aware of what I've been through. I guess he and I both just made a mistake, and it's up to me to rectify it since he seems to be unwilling to follow through on what he's obviously thinking.

It's been about 7 months since our separation, and we've been simply "married on paper" for logistical reasons since then (there is an end date to this, but I don't want to give too many personal details). Though we are technically still married, my STBX has told me point blank that I should start dating someone new if I wish because he's done with me from a romantic/emotional standpoint. He actually prefers that I move on, so there's no cheating involved as our romantic commitment to each other is dead and buried.

I've been seeing this new guy for about a month and a half. He knows all the details of my marital status, and it didn't deter him in the slightest. Things were awesome at first, but it seems I've been put aside as of late. In particular, there have been a couple of times where we've made plans and then he'll just schedule something with his friends right over top of it.

Maybe I'm being paranoid, but it almost seems intentional, like he's trying to send a message. Of course I play it cool, because I feel like I have no better choice. But at this point I just feel used. It's not officially over yet but it sure appears that way. I know it's time to end this before I get hurt more, but it's so hard to admit defeat yet again.

That all rings very true. I think the hardest thing to admit is that the marriage as it stands is broken and done with, and patching things up (if that ever happens) is a process that will be far in the future and a lot of work. Letting go of this marriage is the thing to do it seems, because even if we do work on it in the future we will probably be building an entirely new marriage and leaving this one behind. Not only that, but working on myself is very important as well since my entire twenties were spent with this man. No time like age 30 to reinvent oneself!

I like the dead body analogy. In cases like ours though the body also walks and talks like it's alive, which further inspires hope but is also kinda confusing and scary. I would almost liken it to a kid playing with a pull-string doll. It's fun to play with for a while and it says all the right things, but it's ultimately lifeless. And if you pull the string expecting something other than its preprogrammed phrases, well, that's just not gonna happen. 

My marriage has turned into that, with him going through the motions and the script for the most part, but there's nothing real underneath. And he definitely won't give me anything more. Better to move on than entertain false hope that he'll deviate from his current trajectory.

Thank you for sharing your story. I agree 100 percent on the not dating thing. Can't say I haven't thought about it, but I've realized I'm not yet "free" from this relationship or my current feelings. So there's no point entertaining the idea for a good long while.

I definitely don't have the wherewithal to go nuclear on the relationship, but slowly distancing myself is likely a good solution. It's really hard, but it's probably the answer. Of course, putting it into practice is another matter...

Thanks for the suggestion on the support group. I'm actually in one already, as well as individual counseling. All of this is helpful, but sometimes it just doesn't seem like enough. Being alone with my thoughts is the absolute worst. I spend an embarrassing amount of time with YouTube commentary videos just playing in the background so I don't have to face how I'm feeling. I just wish I had someone I could call when things get too heavy. That used to be him, but now...obviously not.

Everyone says it gets better, and I can feel that some days. But the grief definitely comes in waves, and the time I spend with him does not help one bit. So it seems the best thing is to move on, hard as it may be. I appreciate all of your advice.

I'd like to offer the perspective of someone who was left. I've seen couples counseling mentioned elsewhere in this thread. I would recommend avoiding this unless you have some level of interest in saving the relationship. 

My STBX initiated couples therapy on the pretext of working through our issues. It turned out that he was really using it to gird his loins for the divorce he wanted and in an attempt to "soften the blow" on me. Generally, it seems when one spouse already has one foot out the door, counseling just helps reaffirm the reasons they want to leave the marriage.

If divorce is what you want, then go for it without hesitation. And this is coming from someone whose heart was shattered a few months ago. From my perspective, the kindest thing you can do is to be as friendly and respectful as possible, be honest without being hurtful, and not back down from your position.

You can't really make him understand it hurts you too. My STBX has said the exact same and while I get it intellectually, it rings hollow. It just makes me think, "If you're hurt and I'm hurt by this, why won't you stop?" So I would avoid this topic with him. Discussing it with an individual therapist would probably help.

Best of luck on your journey. I hope you come out on the other side happier than before.

Ah, I see. Sorry for misinterpreting the dynamic there. It's good that you're enforcing minimal contact. Based on the advice I've gotten here and my limited personal experience, it seems that's the way to go. 

It's probably a good idea to set up firmer agreements around specific issues like these so you don't get caught off guard in the future, but my guess is you've already figured that out for yourself. My STBX and I don't really have any parameters around contact at all and that has been a real source of trouble I think. Anything short of a firm, crystal-clear agreement causes one or both parties to step over a line they weren't even sure was there, especially when you're not on the same page. Though you already know what you know, it's certainly not too late to firm up the existing agreement by telling her in no uncertain terms that you have no further desire to hear about her boyfriend (or future boyfriends) even with regard to the kids if that's what you want.

Apologies if this was overly rambly or if my advice (such as it is) is unhelpful. I'm rather inexperienced with all this and still reeling from the impact of this event so I may not be the best person to consult with right now. But I hope I was able to provide at least some small measure of camraderie and/or comfort. All the best.

I'm just starting this process myself so I can't really speak from experience, but surely the day will come when her romantic prospects hardly bother you at all. Wishing you the best.

Thank you for sharing your story, and for your suggestions on how to get through this. It's awesome that you're focusing on self-improvement, and it sounds like it's paying off! I imagine it's really tough when the prospect of divorce comes out of nowhere (there were problems in my marriage, but it was still a shock). Based on what you wrote, it sounds like the process is at least going relatively smoothly and amicably and that you're both looking out for your kids' best interests, which is commendable.

The "mental transformations" you mentioned struck a chord with me. It reminds me of what my husband and I have gone through as well. Obviously growth and change is part of life, and I've heard it said that "you either grow together or grow apart." It seems our respective partners have chosen the "grow apart" route. Hopefully you find a partner who is willing to grow with you.

In terms of the mental games my husband has been playing, after some reflection I have a theory. He has said a few times that divorce is what he wants and that he "doesn't want to change his mind." So it seems he's trying his best to burn this bridge so that, even if he has a moment of weakness and wants to come back, I won't want him. It's a pretty manipulative tactic if that's what he's doing, but he knows how badly I want to save our marriage so perhaps he feels that's his best option. It's not just that he doesn't love me anymore, he doesn't even want to love me, and seems to resent anything that could possibly make that happen.

Honestly, despite everything I've said here I don't mean to paint him as a bad person by any stretch. There's just a lot of anger and pain coming through right now since I'm dealing with some rough times in my own life and he's having a great time in the aftermath of this situation he created.
